title: NY State Assembly · District 61
area: Staten Island's North Shore, plus parts of Lower Manhattan and Brooklyn

context.text: Both the Democratic and Republican primaries scheduled for June 23, 2026 were canceled; incumbent Charles Fall (D) and Casey O'Connor-Manasia (R) each advanced without appearing on a primary ballot. O'Connor-Manasia had also sought the Conservative Party line, but that primary was canceled and she is not listed as a Conservative Party candidate on the general-election ballot.

candidates.name: Charles Fall
candidates.currentRole: NY State Assembly Member, District 61 (since 2019); Assembly Deputy Majority Leader

summary.text: Charles Fall is the incumbent Democratic Assembly Member for District 61 and the Assembly's Deputy Majority Leader, first elected in 2018. The son of immigrants from Guinea, West Africa, he grew up on Staten Island's North Shore, worked in New York City government before the Assembly, and is the first Muslim and first African American Assembly Member elected from Staten Island.

background.text: Fall comes from a working-class family of six; his parents immigrated to Staten Island from Guinea, West Africa. In a 2018 Ballotpedia survey he said he was born and raised on the North Shore.
He earned a BA from Southwestern College in Kansas and a Master of Public Administration with honors from Pace University. According to the Assembly biography, he played college basketball.

In 2014 he served as Staten Island Borough Director and Citywide Islamic Liaison for the Mayor of New York City, working on Universal Pre-K and paid sick leave, then became Chief of Staff to the Staten Island Parks and Recreation Commissioner.
In a 2018 Ballotpedia survey, Fall said he had founded a non-profit that works with young people on options beyond college, including apprenticeships and trade school.

He won the September 2018 Democratic primary for the open Assembly District 61 seat with 43.2% of the vote and the November 2018 general election with 84.0%; he succeeded Matthew Titone and took office in January 2019.

Fall is the Assembly's Deputy Majority Leader. His 2025-2026 committee assignments are Aging; Cities; Consumer Affairs and Protection; Corporations, Authorities and Commissions; Governmental Employees; and Tourism, Parks, Arts and Sports Development.

The Assembly biography says his legislative priorities include resources for teachers, parents, and students, affordable housing, health coverage, and transportation infrastructure; it describes the district as covering the North Shore of Staten Island, Lower Manhattan, and parts of Brooklyn.
He resides in his childhood neighborhood of Mariners Harbor, Staten Island, with his two daughters, according to the Assembly biography; he hosts youth basketball clinics on the North Shore.

priorities.text: 1. Transportation; 2. Education & Youth Programming; 3. Health Care & the Opioid Epidemic.

"Unreliable public transportation, being priced out of a home, and deciding between quality health care and paying rent... We need leaders in Albany who will fight for our community and for our future."
"For far to long, the politics of Albany have failed the voters... As a Member of the Assembly, I will hold my self, and my staff, to the highest ethical standard."

positions.summary: Sponsors legislation to exempt Staten Island and lower Manhattan residents from the Manhattan congestion-pricing surcharge, and said he welcomed Governor Hochul's 2024 pause of congestion pricing implementation, citing the financial burden on constituents.
positions.quote: I have had concerns about the rollout of the MTA's congestion pricing plan, as it clearly imposed an additional financial burden on our residents... Governor Hochul's decision to pause this plan is a positive step.

record.text: Serves as Assembly Deputy Majority Leader; assigned to the Aging, Cities, Consumer Affairs and Protection, Corporations/Authorities and Commissions, Governmental Employees, and Tourism/Parks/Arts and Sports Development committees.

Prime sponsor of A09590-A, authorizing the state Dormitory Authority to finance construction of New York Climate Exchange facilities on Governors Island; passed the Assembly and Senate and was delivered to the Governor on September 22, 2026.
Prime sponsor of A02144, which would exempt residents of lower Manhattan and Staten Island from the Manhattan congestion-pricing surcharge; referred to committee, no floor vote as of September 2026.
Prime sponsor of A02099, which would exempt Staten Island residents from Verrazzano-Narrows Bridge tolls; referred to committee, no floor vote as of September 2026.

Prime sponsor of A10136, extending through December 2027 the authorization for Staten Island residents in high-risk brush-fire areas to cut and remove reeds from their property; passed the Assembly and was delivered to the Senate.

Issued a statement on the crisis in Gaza saying he 'unequivocally condemned the violence that claimed innocent lives on October 7' while calling the destruction in Gaza 'devastating and unjustifiable' and urging immediate, unrestricted humanitarian aid.

candidates.name: Casey O'Connor-Manasia

summary.text: Casey O'Connor-Manasia is the Republican candidate challenging incumbent Charles Fall in Assembly District 61.

background.text: Ballotpedia lists O'Connor-Manasia as the Republican candidate for Assembly District 61; the Republican primary scheduled for June 23, 2026 was canceled and she advanced to the general election.

candidates.researchNotes: No Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey response or campaign website could be located for O'Connor-Manasia as of September 25, 2026. The Staten Island Republican and Staten Island Young Republican organizations publicized their endorsement of her candidacy on Facebook, but those posts contain no policy statements from the candidate herself, so no positions or priorities are included here.
